title: Enterprise service bus (ESB) and SOAP in legacy environments

videos.script: In 2015 Serra Alta bought a bus. {{bus}} Not one with wheels. An enterprise service bus: IBM Integration Bus, with IBM MQ underneath it. The promise was simple. Every system would connect once, to the bus, and the bus would do the rest. Eleven years later, Joana inherits it. {{flows}} Seventy message flows. Many of them are SOAP services. And a team of four people that every project has to wait for. This lesson starts with why companies bought buses, and the arithmetic that made the promise sound right. {{count}} Then it opens a SOAP message. The envelope, the header, the body, the fault, and the WSDL contract that describes them. {{envelope}} Then it looks at what went wrong. Business rules moved into the bus, one reasonable request at a time, and the integration team became a queue. {{queue}} The last two sections are the ones you will use at work. How a modern service talks to a SOAP system without catching its habits. And how to shrink a bus, flow by flow, without switching off something that runs once a year. {{shrink}}
